In the implementation of `TypeHandler.createValue`, there is a conditional block that checks various predefined class types and performs conversions accordingly. If the provided class is not one of the predefined types, the method will return `null` at the end of the method.

This behavior aligns with the observation in the current bug report that the method may return `null` for unknown classes instead of throwing a `ParseException`. The root cause of the failure lies in the conditional block at the end of the `createValue` method that handles unknown class types by returning `null`.
